facts: Azure portal = web-based unified console at portal.azure.com to build, manage, monitor resources
Customizable dashboards; accessible from any browser and OS, no install
Azure mobile app (iOS/Android) manages resources from a phone
Portal blades: Monitor (health/metrics), Defender for Cloud (security recs), Marketplace (VM images, 3rd-party appliances)
GUI-based; use CLI/PowerShell/ARM for automation and repeatability

pick.when: manage all Azure resources via a web URL
buy/deploy third-party virtual security appliance
manage a web app from an iPhone
pick.use: Azure mobile app or Azure portal (browser)

pick.when: browse available VM images
view security recommendations

traps: Azure Monitor is for health/metrics, not security recommendations
Portal is GUI; not the right answer for scripted repeatable deployments

facts: Cloud Shell = browser-based, authenticated shell in portal or shell.azure.com; supports Bash and PowerShell
Azure CLI: cross-platform commands (az ...), runs on Windows, macOS, Linux
Azure PowerShell: Az module cmdlets (verb-noun), cross-platform with PowerShell 7
Cloud Shell has CLI and PowerShell preinstalled; needs no local install; uses Azure Files storage for persistence
Use CLI/PowerShell scripts for automating tasks; works from any device with a browser (tablet, Android)

pick.when: manage Azure from a browser on any device without installing tools
run az commands on Windows, macOS, Linux
automate with cmdlets in PowerShell
create a VM from an Android tablet
pick.use: Azure portal, Cloud Shell, or Azure mobile app

traps: Cloud Shell is not a local install; it is browser-hosted
Azure CLI is not Windows-only

facts: Azure Arc extends Azure management to on-premises, multi-cloud and edge resources
Projects non-Azure resources into Azure Resource Manager as Azure resources
Manage Windows/Linux servers, Kubernetes clusters, SQL Server, data services via Azure portal
Lets you apply Azure Policy, tags, RBAC, Monitor and Defender to non-Azure resources
Run Azure data services on-premises or other clouds with Arc-enabled data services

pick.when: manage on-premises Windows Server from the Azure portal
unified way to project non-Azure resources into ARM
govern servers/Kubernetes across on-premises and other clouds
consistent multi-cloud and on-premises management platform

traps: Not Azure Migrate (that assesses and migrates workloads)
Not Azure Stack HCI/Hub, which is hardware/infrastructure, not a management plane

facts: IaC = manage and provision infrastructure through machine-readable definition files instead of manual steps
Gives consistent, repeatable, version-controllable deployments
Azure native IaC: ARM templates (JSON) and Bicep (declarative, simpler syntax)
ARM templates and Bicep are idempotent and declarative
Azure DevOps/GitHub provide version control and pipelines to deploy IaC

pick.when: repeatedly deploy and remove many identically configured VMs from templates
version control tools to manage code
simpler syntax than JSON for Azure deployments

traps: Azure DevOps manages code and pipelines; it is not itself the template language
Declarative IaC states desired end state, not step-by-step commands

facts: ARM is the deployment and management service for Azure; all tools (portal, CLI, PowerShell, SDK, REST) call it
Resource groups are logical containers for related resources; resource can be in only one group
ARM templates are declarative JSON files describing resources to deploy
Templates are idempotent and reusable, giving consistent deployments across environments
Deploys resources in correct dependency order and in parallel where possible
Azure Policy defines rules for what can be deployed; ARM templates define what to deploy

pick.when: automate creation of the same 20 resources for each business unit
consistent, repeatable deployment of resources across environments
group, organize and manage resources with shared lifecycle
enforce rules on what resources may be deployed

traps: Azure Policy restricts/audits; it does not deploy resources
Resource locks and tags do not automate deployment

facts: Azure Advisor is a free personalized cloud consultant giving best-practice recommendations
Five categories: Reliability, Security, Performance, Cost, Operational Excellence
Identifies underutilized or idle resources, e.g. VMs, to cut cost
Recommends VMs not protected by Azure Backup, and reserved instance savings
Recommendations based on your resource configuration and usage telemetry
Compare usage against best practices; Advisor score shows adherence

pick.when: identify underutilized or unused VMs
compare cloud usage to best practices
recommendations to improve cost, security, reliability, performance
VMs not protected by Azure Backup

traps: Advisor recommends; it does not enforce (Azure Policy enforces)
Not Service Health, which reports Azure platform incidents

facts: Azure Service Health = Azure status + Service Health + Resource Health
Azure status: global view of Azure service health, public, no sign-in
Service Health: personalized view of service issues, planned maintenance, health advisories for your subscriptions/regions
Resource Health: health of your individual resources, e.g. a specific VM
Configure Service Health alerts to be notified of incidents and planned maintenance
Planned maintenance events appear in Service Health

pick.when: notified of planned Microsoft maintenance affecting your subscription
view service outage notifications affecting a VM's region
health of a specific resource such as a VM
global Azure status for all regions

traps: Azure Monitor is for your resource metrics/logs, not Microsoft platform incidents
Advisor gives recommendations, not outage notices

facts: Azure Monitor collects, analyzes and acts on telemetry from Azure and on-premises
Two data types: metrics (numeric) and logs
Log Analytics: query logs with KQL in a Log Analytics workspace; central repository for events from multiple resources
Alerts proactively notify or trigger actions via action groups (email, SMS, webhook)
Application Insights: APM for live web apps; detects performance anomalies
Activity Log: subscription-level control-plane events (who did what, e.g. stopped a VM); kept 90 days

pick.when: collect events from many resources into one central repository
auto-send alert when admin stops a VM
monitor performance of a live web app
see which user turned off a VM
run queries across log data

traps: Activity Log holds 90 days; older needs export to a workspace
Azure Monitor is not Service Health (platform incidents) or Advisor (recommendations)

facts: SLA = Microsoft's commitment to uptime/connectivity, expressed as a percentage (e.g. 99.9%)
Composite SLA = multiply the SLAs of dependent services together
Composite SLA is lower than the lowest individual SLA when services are chained serially
Higher SLA comes from redundancy, e.g. Availability Zones or multiple regions
Free services and preview services have no financial SLA
Violating an SLA gives service credits; more nines means less allowed downtime

pick.when: app depends on web app 99.95% and SQL DB 99.99%
increase availability beyond a single instance
pick.use: Deploy across Availability Zones or regions

pick.when: VM with premium SSD single instance
VMs in two or more Availability Zones

traps: Composite SLA is not the average or the highest value
Adding a dependency lowers the composite SLA; adding redundancy raises it

facts: Private preview: invite-only for selected customers
Public preview: available to all customers; also called public beta
Preview services are excluded from SLAs and may have limited or no support
Public preview often offered at reduced price; terms in preview supplemental terms
General availability (GA): released for production use, covered by SLA and support
Typical path: private preview, public preview, then GA
Modern Lifecycle Policy: minimum 12 months notice before end of support if no successor (excludes free/preview)

pick.when: evaluate a new feature before release, available to anyone
service with production SLA and full support
limited invited customers evaluate feature

traps: Preview services are not covered by SLA
Private preview is invite-only; public preview is open to all

facts: Plans: Basic (free), Developer, Standard, Professional Direct, Premier/Unified
Basic: included for all; billing/subscription support, 24/7 self-help, Advisor, Service Health
Basic cannot open technical support requests; paid plans can
Developer, Standard, Professional Direct allow technical support tickets
Standard and above add 24/7 access to support engineers; Premier adds TAM and architecture help
Support plan is per subscription; Pro Direct and Premier offer architectural guidance

pick.when: open technical support request
pick.use: Developer, Standard, Professional Direct or Premier

pick.when: free, billing and subscription issues only
architectural review from Microsoft at least cost
designated technical account manager

traps: Basic cannot open technical tickets; it can only open billing/subscription cases
Support plans do not change service SLAs

facts: Azure Active Directory is now Microsoft Entra ID
Azure Security Center and Azure Defender are now Microsoft Defender for Cloud
Azure Sentinel is now Microsoft Sentinel
Azure Blueprints bundled ARM templates, RBAC, policy and locks; being retired, replaced by template specs and deployment stacks
Azure Germany: separate sovereign cloud, closed and migrated to global Azure regions
Classic administrator roles (Co-administrator, Service Administrator) retired in favor of Azure RBAC

pick.when: package templates, policies, RBAC into repeatable environment (legacy)
replace Azure Active Directory name
cloud security posture management (formerly Security Center)

traps: Azure Germany was not limited to German residents and is no longer an active offering
Old exams use old names; map them to Entra, Defender for Cloud, Sentinel
